The active site lies in a groove between domains I and II. The catalytic dyad consists of Cys145 (nucleophile) and His41 (general base). The oxyanion hole is formed by backbone NHs of Gly143, Ser144, and Cys145 — these stabilize the tetrahedral intermediate during substrate cleavage and also form hydrogen bonds with fragment carbonyl or sulfonyl groups. Key subsites: S1 (His163, Glu166/Phe140 backbones — prefers small H-bond acceptors like lactams, pyridones, or pyrazoles), S2 (His41, Met49, Met165 — a hydrophobic pocket that accommodates medium-sized aromatics and aliphatic groups), S1' (shallow and solvent-exposed — tolerates diverse substituents), and S4 (Gln189, flexible and partially solvent-exposed). About 40% of confirmed fragment hits bind covalently. Electrophilic warheads react with the Cys145 thiolate: chloroacetamides are the most common (SN2 displacement of chloride), followed by acrylamides (Michael addition) and vinyl sulfonamides. The remaining ~60% bind non-covalently through H-bond networks with the oxyanion hole and S1 pocket residues, plus hydrophobic packing against Met49 and Met165 in S2.
